reason: The heart and blood vessels seem like the starting point for a returning blood circuit.

alternatives.reason: Breathing muscles and lungs should provide a way to move air, but I chose to build the blood route first.

effect: The result confirms that the heart and vessels form a returning circulation that can carry supplies to cells. I still need a way to move air into the lungs.
reaction: The explanation of the returning route makes the combination clear.

expectation: I expect the muscles to help move air into and out of the lungs, though I do not yet know how the model will connect them to circulation.

effect: The breathing muscles move air to lung spaces beside tiny blood vessels, and the new goal is to connect that air supply to circulation.
reaction: The distinction between moving air and moving blood makes the two combinations easier to understand.
reason: This is the only offered combination and directly addresses the new goal.
expectation: I expect the lungs and circulation to form a route for oxygen to enter the blood, though I am unsure how the exchange will be explained.

effect: The result completes the route: oxygen enters blood in the lungs, blood returns to the heart and travels to the body, and carbon dioxide returns to the lungs to be breathed out.
reaction: The full route clarified how breathing and circulation work together.

mostWorthwhile.text: Connecting the breathing lungs to circulation was most worthwhile because the result explains gas exchange and traces the blood's route through the heart, lungs and body.

leastWorthwhile.text: Making breathing lungs was less informative on its own: it describes changing chest space but leaves how the breathing muscles produce that change unexplained.

surprise.text: The completed route made clear that blood passes through the heart between the lungs and the rest of the body.

arbitrary.text: None of the combinations felt arbitrary; each matched an explicit goal, though the compatible options were supplied rather than discovered.

continue.text: I would continue for another chapter to see how the oxygen supply connects to the arm's work. The explanations have been clear, though completing these steps does not establish that students understand them.
